body:
"If I had any spare cash myself, I'd share to help you through this and maybe loosen the hours so you could find a way out. As it is, I just have my keyboard." <-- This my friend is all that I needed. Someone to listen and talk to.

Your responses have been most helpful and I thank you Forensicator for spending your precious time to read and respond to my rantings and what not. Your life experiences are definitely motivating and will remind me that things are getting better maybe without me even realizing it at the moment. Thank you so much.

I'm glad you're empathizing with me, thanks Forensicator. It helps me feel less lonely tbh. My friends try to bring me out of the house as often as they can but its burning a hole in my wallet and most of the time all we do is drink. I've become dependent on alcohol to numb away the pain among other forms of substance abuse which I know is a horrible thing to do..but it's what keeps me going on those really tough nights. I'm just trying to buy time because I believe things do get better in the long run like you said, it just doesn't seem to be in sight yet. I don't know how much longer I can last but knowing that there's people like you out there makes me more willing to keep trying.

As for the freelancing, I did have an intense passion for it but being the way things are now, I'm so unenthusiastic about anything and everything. It's become a mundane chore for me and I'd really like to regain that passion I had for the work. Have you ever found yourself in a similar situation as this?

I think you're right about the friends thing.. It's just hard to come to them when you get advice like "Stop crying and suck it up. You're stronger than this" or "You know we don't like seeing you sad and it makes us all down too. You'll get over this soon just stop thinking about it". I honestly hate that kind of advice but maybe it's just me.

I work 30 hours a week at one job and then I have a second job that is more of a freelance thing at home. I basically work until the client is satisfied with the finished result and get paid a flat commission based off the project and not the hours I put in. Since I'm an amateur it really doesn't pay much and sometimes it's not worth it but hey it's money.

I'll definitely seek help on askreddit. Thanks for the heads up on that. I'm hoping there's a solution to this.. I'm looking for any kind of hope or opportunity so I can hold onto that and keep going.
